we have developed methods for (1) automatically classifying pieces of music in terms a three-dimensional resonance-arousing-valence model of emotion; (2) predicting a listener’s current emotional state on the basis of a sequence of pieces that he or she recently listened to; and (3), given a listener’s current or predicted emotional state, selecting a ranked list pieces of music that best match the state.

we have developed a set of methods and techniques that are useful in a number of different scenarios and that can be used in conjunction with one another to produce an effective and efficient music-recommendation system.

we provide a new model for the representation, classification, prediction, and recommendation of music in terms that relate directly to emotion, and we demonstrate that this model is effective in practice.
we have proposed a new model for representing the emotion expressed in music and we have proposed a number of methods for using this model in music recommendation.
we have proposed a new model for the representation and prediction of emotional states associated with music, which we have applied in a possible recommendation scenario.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the emotional states of listeners can be modeled in a principled way and used to improve the recommendation of music.
